title: Request fingerprinting + adaptive backfill to cut embedding tail latency
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: reduce p99/p995 tail latency for the embeddings endpoint (hosted + dedicated) without hurting average throughput. We suspect a combination of request-level fingerprinting and adaptive backfill (opportunistic packing of small requests into idle microbatch slots) plus lightweight kernel hints will reduce long tails caused by stragglers and small singleton requests.

Scope: prototype a non-invasive fingerprinting layer that classifies incoming requests (model, vector-dim, token-length, requester-type, priority) and use that fingerprint to make two runtime decisions: 1) whether to backfill idle batch slots with compatible small requests, and 2) which kernel variant (quantized fast-path vs compatibility kernel) to prefer for each microbatch. The prototype should include telemetry, canary rollout, and a follow-up plan for making heuristics data-driven.

Non-goals: global scheduling rewrite, changes to customer-visible batching API, or new billing model changes for now.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for embeddings requests under mixed workload must improve at least 30% on the reference replay (95th/99th/99.9th snapshots included)
No >5% regression in average throughput (tokens/sec) on dedicated pools during A/B canary
Fallbacks must exist: disable backfill via flag and ensure behavior returns to baseline without data loss
End-to-end regression tests and a small production canary are running before roll-out to all regions
tasks: Design request fingerprint schema and matching rules (Aisha, 1d)
Implement lightweight fingerprinting middleware in ingress runtime (Marco, 3d)
Add adaptive backfill queue logic to microbatch dispatcher with safety limits (Marco + Jin, 5d)
Expose kernel hint flags from dispatcher to serving runtime (Marco + Elena, 4d)
Create replay harness and metrics dashboard for before/after comparison (SRE + Data Eng, 3d)
Run scoped canary on dedicated-qa pool and collect p50/p95/p99/p999 (1 week)
risks: Backfill could increase head-of-line blocking if matching rules are too permissive
Incorrect kernel hints may cause slight quality regressions on some quantized paths
Telemetry gaps could make it hard to attribute improvement to a single change
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag and operator-visible binary (start off)
Internal canary on dedicated-qa with synthetic mixed workloads (3 days)
Small production canary (5% traffic) for 7 days, monitor p99/p999 and error rate
Gradual ramp to 25% then 50% then global if metrics meet acceptance criteria
Kill switch: runtime flag + circuit breaker in dispatcher
monitoring_success_metrics: p50/p95/p99/p999 latency time series by model and pool
notes: Design consideration: prefer conservative matching at first (exact model + dim + small token len window) then relax based on hit-rate
We should capture a small sample payloads for replay; ensure PII stripping before storage
Compare against existing opportunistic coalescer experiments (see ENG-47210) to avoid duplicated work
If we see regression on average latency, explore a hybrid time-window threshold instead of hard backfill
